title: Register Convention: What Is Still Available on a Registration Already Spent From
content:
Where a spend already stands among the entries of a registration under the Belrose Trade-In and Upgrade Programmes, what is still available to put toward a sale is read as this convention directs, and the reading turns on whether the programme allows its credit to be spent in parts.

## The convention

Where a spend already stands among the registration's entries and the programme allows the credit to be spent in parts, the credit still available is read as the sum of every entry booked to the registration that moves the credit. Where a spend already stands among those entries and the programme does not allow the credit to be spent in parts, nothing is left to put toward the sale. Where no spend stands among the entries, the credit still available is read as the credit the registration shows as issued.

An entry moves the credit where it books the credit, revalues it upward, spends it or takes it away; a valuation entry and an inspection entry move nothing, whatever amount they carry. Spends and forfeits carry negative amounts.

| Programme | Credit may be spent in parts |
|---|---|
| Belrose Standard Trade-In | no |
| Diamond Trade-Up Guarantee | no |
| Bridal Upgrade Guarantee | yes |
| Lifetime Diamond Upgrade Guarantee | yes |
| Signature Collection Upgrade Privilege | yes |
| Estate Purchase and Consignment Programme | yes |

## Readings on hypothetical entries

A registration shows 5000 USD issued and carries a credit entry of 5000 USD, a revaluation of 250 USD and a spend of 1200 USD.

- Under the Signature Collection Upgrade Privilege: 5000 plus 250 less 1200, which is 4050 USD.
- Under the Belrose Standard Trade-In: nothing is left to put toward the sale.
- With no spend among the entries at all: the 5000 USD the registration shows as issued.
